canonical_bindings.use: Separates product, capability, system, evidence, lifecycle, and residue claims.
Keeps canonical meanings distinct from candidate records and generated presentation.
Keeps the Essays coordination identity distinct from its product, DomainSpec project, repository path, and runtime.
Shapes the candidate Essays value proposition without treating it as product proof.
Requires Essays to cross exact semantic and generated-system stages before implementation claims.
Defines what Essays must enable independently of Whisper, editor framework, UI, or runtime realization.

proposals.normative_voice: Essays is the CyberAlchemy v2 subproduct that enables a writer to develop long-form audience-facing text through attributable intent, explicit composition artifacts, addressable review, revision decisions, bounded validation, visible editorial residue, and clean export while preserving human editorial authority.
proposals.plain_language_voice: Essays is a focused writing product that keeps the reasons, feedback, changes, and open questions behind a draft connected to the text.
proposals.domain_context_voice: Inside CyberAlchemy v2, Essays owns product meaning for the writing experience. Whisper and any editor or runtime are replaceable realizations and retain their own source ownership.
proposals.owner_route: Essays Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
proposals.forbidden_collapse: The Essays Product is not the Essays Project, Goal, Whisper spell, editor substrate, runtime process, frontend, draft, or publication channel.

proposals.normative_voice: An Essay Workspace is the bounded local carrier that keeps one essay's author intent, transport, composition artifacts, draft revisions, sources, addressable reviews, validation reports, export records, and editorial residue under one stable identity.
proposals.plain_language_voice: An Essay Workspace keeps the draft and the important work behind it together.
proposals.domain_context_voice: The Essays runtime may persist and project a Workspace, but the Workspace is not a CAV2-D60 Project and does not own product or authority decisions.
proposals.forbidden_collapse: An Essay Workspace is not a CyberAlchemy Project, repository, chat thread, raw filesystem directory, publication, or authority container.

proposals.normative_voice: A Reviewable Essay is a version-identified draft whose audience-facing text, authoring-only state, evidence gaps, review anchors, revision history, validation posture, and unresolved residue are inspectable without treating any review or validator as editorial authority.
proposals.plain_language_voice: A Reviewable Essay is a draft whose text, feedback, changes, and remaining concerns can be inspected together.
proposals.domain_context_voice: Reviewability is an Essays product outcome, not proof that the prose is correct, valuable, publishable, or accepted by its author.
proposals.owner_route: Essay author plus Essays Product Capability owner
proposals.forbidden_collapse: A Reviewable Essay is not a final publication, validation PASS, accepted review, product-value result, or authority decision.

proposals.normative_voice: An Addressable Editorial Review is a set of feedback records bound to stable artifact and text locations, each preserving the selected text or scope, issue type, requested change, reviewer, priority, lifecycle state, and author disposition.
proposals.plain_language_voice: Addressable review keeps every comment attached to the exact part of the draft it concerns and records what happened to it.
proposals.domain_context_voice: Essays adopts Whisper's review-addressability requirement while keeping reviewer feedback, author response, and automatic diagnostics as separate claims.
proposals.forbidden_collapse: A review comment is not an accepted revision, author intent, validator result, or permission to change text.

proposals.normative_voice: Editorial Residue is a named unresolved remainder in an Essay Workspace, such as missing evidence, disputed wording, deferred feedback, uncertain intent, unproved transport behavior, or an intentionally rejected revision, with an owner and next route.
proposals.plain_language_voice: Editorial residue is what the writing process still does not know or has deliberately left unresolved.
proposals.domain_context_voice: Essays preserves residue so a clean draft does not erase uncertainty or inflate a claim beyond its evidence.
proposals.owner_route: Essay author plus the owner of the unresolved claim
proposals.forbidden_collapse: Editorial Residue is not a hidden error, automatic task, permission to guess, or proof that the essay is incomplete for its intended use.

proposals.normative_voice: A Product Model View is a version-identified, read-only projection of the definitions, products, projects, and ontologies that govern or contextualize one Essays runtime candidate, preserving each record's identity, status, meaning, owner route, provenance, boundary, and source epoch.
proposals.plain_language_voice: The Product Model View shows what Essays means, who owns that meaning, and which source the screen is describing.
proposals.domain_context_voice: Essays may expose this view so a writer or builder can inspect the product construction context without leaving the local runtime. The view is generated from bound semantic sources and never becomes their authority.
proposals.owner_route: Essays Product Capability owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 ontology owners
proposals.forbidden_collapse: A Product Model View is not a definition registry, ontology runtime, Project, editor, acceptance decision, mutation surface, or proof that its projected records are admitted or current beyond the displayed source epoch.
